basis: Site-unspecified malignant neoplasm; no organ of origin is assignable. CNS examples among children do not establish the site across this umbrella.
Carcinoma arising in breast, which has no axis; estrogen receptor expression does not establish endocrine gland disease.
Congenital nasal dermoid involving cutaneous or subcutaneous tissue; nose falls within the pulmonary axis.
Congenital neutropenia with impaired host defense; recurrent gingival inflammation affects 4/4 reported patients.
Neoplasm of the junction between medulla and cervical spinal cord.
Lysosomal disease with defining neurodevelopmental dysfunction; muscle hypoplasia 80-99%, skeletal disease and skin ulcers 30-79%; nystagmus alone does not establish eye damage.
Inherited skeletal muscle energy metabolism disorder with AMP deaminase deficiency and muscle weakness; erythrocyte enzyme deficiency alone lacks clinical blood disease.
Defining skeletal malformations, nail dysplasia and dental/oral anomalies, generally present in 80-99%; cardiac disease is not characteristic.
Malignant cells directly occupy leptomeninges and subarachnoid space; the variable primary cancer site is not assigned.
Disease of the vitreous body of the eye.
Defining developmental and skin disease; exotropia 4/4, joint hypermobility and weakness 2/4 support eye and joint dysfunction; dental caries is separately diagnosed.
Pyrimidine metabolism disorder; intellectual disability 12/19 and seizures 30-79%; feeding problems alone do not establish GI injury, and villous atrophy occurs in 5-29%.
Progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy; cardiomyopathy commonly affects roughly 30-50%; respiratory muscle weakness does not itself establish lung damage.
Ketogenesis/leucine disorder; hepatic injury with transaminase elevation in 14/20 and frequent hepatocyte lipid accumulation; developmental delay 17/35; crisis symptoms add no axes.
Congenital hypoplasia or absence of finger phalanges defines this skeletal malformation.
Mediastinal ganglioneuroblastoma arises from peripheral sympathetic neural tissue; mediastinal location does not establish lung involvement.
Pneumoconiosis caused by inhaled silica and iron-containing dust, producing pulmonary deposition and fibrosis.
Defining upper-limb phocomelia, encephalocele and thrombocytopenia occur in 80-99%; urinary abnormalities occur in only 5-29%, with other urogenital findings reproductive.
Macular retinal pigment epithelial dystrophy with patterned lipofuscin accumulation and retinal degeneration.
Defining severe skeletal thoracic dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia commonly causes early death and brain defects are described as common; visceral cysts lack evidence of >=30% frequency.
Gonococcal infection directly damages the cornea; skin-related ancestors do not establish cutaneous involvement.
Corpus callosum demyelination defines the disease; alcoholism, malnutrition and vitamin deficiency are associated conditions rather than additional organ damage caused by it.
Isolated congenital underdevelopment of the tongue; tongue and oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited abnormal hemoglobin causes methemoglobinemia and impaired blood oxygen carriage; cyanosis alone does not establish skin or cardiopulmonary damage.
Malignant neoplasm involving the central nervous system; lymphoma is only one subtype and does not justify an immune axis across the umbrella.
